one_recommended_comparator.basis: Published Algorithm1 exact-gradient version0 and section5.1 K-overlap extension; optional feature sharing disabled.
one_recommended_comparator.budget: Same state/roles/horizon is not equal compute. The mathematical schedule needs4 native current-state forwards per iteration, no private probes/query virtual forwards. Any implementation must prospectively meter exact forward/backward/checkpoint/serving/resource work; no source or resource plan is created here.
faithfulness_limits: Published loss, ownership and probability aggregation are preserved. The shared backbone, native graph, common400 warm state, role weighting, H16 and SGD rates adapt the published independent image-model experiment.
Use exact KL via log_softmax; the author code clamps probabilities at1e-10, an explicitly disclosed implementation difference near extreme probabilities.
Optional cross-feature masked sums and stochastic labeling are omitted using published version0/core objective; this is not a reproduction of the best feature-sharing/stochastic-label image results.
Nonowner true-label CE is not retained in literal CMCL. Adding the current response method all-member CE anchor would be a different CMCL-inspired control and must not be labeled faithful CMCL.

Different objective/label timing/gradient schedule means a CMCL comparison cannot isolate the finite-response remainder by itself; existing matched first-order/uniform/current-margin/stopped/graph controls remain necessary.
one_recommended_comparator.fixed_setting_rationale: beta.75 is the authenticated author default/example; K3 is a published overlap value and gives3/4 owner supervision, close to authors4/5 example. K4 onM4 would eliminate every nonowner penalty and reduce to ordinary CE; K1 is the original Algorithm1 special case but is not the recommended sole close comparator. These are prospective declared adaptation choices, not graph-optimal or table-winning settings.
one_recommended_comparator.initialization_and_endpoint: Only after current interpretation, a newly reviewed caller could use the same exact common400 state/full24492x300FP32 native graph, same roles, H16 fixed endpoint and four members; no warm acquisition or Adam reactivation, additional expert or intermediate selector.
one_recommended_comparator.name: CMCL exact-KL overlap objective on the matched shared4 native continuation
one_recommended_comparator.node_losses: c_i,m=-log p_m(y_i); d_i,m=KL(U_5||p_m)=-log5-(1/5)sum_c log p_m(c). Score a_i,m=c_i,m-beta*d_i,m, equivalent to authors candidate score after subtracting a model-independent constant.
one_recommended_comparator.owner_step: Choose exactly the three lowest current a_i,m for each training node; fixed member-index tie break, stopped discrete ownership recomputed once per iteration.
one_recommended_comparator.probability_aggregation: Complete unweighted mean of four member softmax probabilities; no confidence routing, winner selection or logit averaging.
one_recommended_comparator.update_loss: L_T=mean_i inT [sum_m v_i,m*c_i,m + beta*(1-v_i,m)*d_i,m]. Use L=(L_S+L_R)/2 to give equal aggregate role mass; this role weighting is an explicit graph adaptation. Compute one shared scalar gradient and all private row gradients at the same incoming state, then simultaneous plain SGD with existing eta_core.001 and eta_private.01.

one_small_graph_extension.alpha_provenance: One prospective untested design constant in loss units, not a CMCL published setting or adopted optimum; no grid.
one_small_graph_extension.definition: Start with ordinary fixed CMCL owners v0. On the existing public graph restricted to permitted training nodes, form row-normalized neighbor owner frequency q_i,m=sum_j A_ij*v0_j,m/sum_j A_ij; isolates use q_i,m=K/M. Replace a_i,m by a_i,m-alpha*q_i,m, then chooseK3 lowest once simultaneously. Stop gradients through v0/q and use the same CE/nonowner-KL update and probability pool.
one_small_graph_extension.falsifiable_decision: After current interpretation and separate review/admission, keep only if actual-edge voting adds pool/net-repair benefit over ordinary CMCL without lowering member competence and the corresponding pre-frozen graph permutation fails to explain it; otherwise reject this extension.
limits: It is one fixed synchronous assignment step, not exact minimization of a coupled graph objective.
Neighbor specialist coherence can reinforce common mistakes; observed shared unanimous-error clustering does not establish that useful specialist identities are homophilous.
The saved graph diagnostic has stronger shared unanimity only in a narrow matched population and no larger general pooled wrong-class recurrence; it does not justify a graph-causal theorem.
Hard assignments can amplify seed/tie artifacts; balances and response-based capacity are not guaranteed.
This is a small antecedent-based graph regularization proposal, not a new generic MoE or a novelty claim.
one_small_graph_extension.name: One synchronous neighbor vote in CMCL owner scores
one_small_graph_extension.why_graph_specific: Nearby training nodes coordinate specialist identity through actual edges. It tests whether graph coherence added to ordinary confidence specialization can explain the purported response benefit.

predictions_for_saved_error_pattern: CMCL can flatten nonowner wrong predictions and reduce NLL/Brier/wrong-answer confidence, making the probability pool more usable without a finite response. Owner CE can create correct evidence through ordinary training.

Current owner ranking uses present CE and confidence, not who will reduce a true-versus-rival margin after learning. For equal high-confidence wrong predictions all scores tie; ownership gives no measured corrective-capacity information.

Flattening predictions can leave the same wrong argmax; the shared core can retain correlated errors. A reduction in confidence or error overlap alone is insufficient evidence of useful complementarity.

Finite response must produce additional net repairs and served-pool quality while preserving member competence beyond this ordinary confidence control; its finite remainder additionally must beat the matched first-order utility control at reported actual cost.
